title: GenieA
tagline: A public-safety platform built with Sylhet Metropolitan Police: one microservice backend behind a citizen app, a police app, and the admin panels that run the operation.

cover.alt: GenieA citizen app: a map of nearby police stations, an emergency button and live location sharing

screens.alt: GenieA citizen app: a map of nearby police stations, an emergency button and live location sharing
GenieA citizen app: the SOS countdown while a help request goes out
GenieA citizen app: connecting to police dispatch, with the caller's location on the map
GenieA police app: an officer's home screen with a live map, duty log and case status
GenieA police app: the live case list, with a reported incident awaiting response
GenieA police app: an officer's duty schedule for the month

gallery.alt: GenieA admin panel: a live dashboard with a city map, SOS calls, incidents and case filters
gallery.caption: Admin panel: the live dashboard

brief: Built in collaboration with Sylhet Metropolitan Police in Bangladesh, GenieA connects citizens and police through dedicated apps.
Citizens can raise an SOS that shares their live location and connects them to dispatch. Officers get live cases, duty logs and shift schedules. Admin panels run the whole operation.
It's used by 10K+ people, and by the police department itself.
myRole: Designed and built the microservice backend that serves all three products.
Split services by job across FastAPI, NestJS and Go, with Redis for caching and RabbitMQ for messaging between them.
Containerised everything with Docker and ran it on Kubernetes.
Ran it end to end, from system design and API contracts to production release.
results: Used by a 10K+ user base and by Sylhet Metropolitan Police.
Live on both the Play Store and the App Store.

title: HealthStar
tagline: An all-in-one healthcare app. I built the MVP from scratch: the microservice backend, the mobile app and the admin panel.

cover.alt: HealthStar: a map of nearby hospitals and blood donors, marked by blood group

screens.alt: HealthStar: a map of nearby hospitals and blood donors, marked by blood group
HealthStar: filtering blood donors by gender, blood group and hospital
HealthStar: an urgent request broadcasting to matching donors nearby

brief: HealthStar is an all-in-one healthcare app, available on the Play Store and the App Store.

At its centre is a blood-donor network: a map of nearby hospitals and donors by blood group, donor filters, and urgent requests broadcast to matching donors nearby. Other tabs cover doctors, a health forum and prescriptions.
myRole: Built the MVP from scratch: the backend, the mobile app and the admin panel.
Used the same microservice approach as GenieA: FastAPI, NestJS and Go services, Redis, RabbitMQ, Docker and Kubernetes.
Development is ongoing.

architecture.caption: Same playbook as GenieA, different patients.

results: MVP shipped to the Play Store and App Store.

title: StarWatch
tagline: Drones built from scratch: sensors for autonomy, AI for mission planning, and live video back to the ground.

cover.alt: The StarWatch team standing behind a row of their quadcopters

gallery.alt: StarWatch test flights at dusk: drones launched by hand, hovering and flying over a field
gallery.caption: Test flights. No drones were harmed (this time).

brief: StarWatch builds drone systems from scratch under Star Technologies.
The goal is automation: drones that sense their surroundings, plan missions with AI, and stream live video back to the ground.
myRole: Embedded systems engineer.
Flight stack: ArduPilot on the flight controller, talking MAVLink to a ROS-based companion computer.
Autonomy from LiDAR, optical flow and sonar, so the drones can hold position and avoid obstacles without relying on GPS alone.
Live video to the ground station over WebRTC, and AI-based mission planning on top.
results: Work in progress. Watch this space (and the sky).

title: Project Altair
tagline: IUT's Mars rover. I wrote the software that let it drive, see, grab things and find its own way.

cover.alt: Rifat on stage at an IUT Robotics Society showcase, with the rover beside him

gallery.alt: The Altair rover with its robotic arm, on display at an exhibition
gallery.caption: The rover and its 6-joint arm

gallery.alt: Team Altair posing with the Bangladesh flag at a rover competition site
gallery.caption: Team Altair in the field

brief: Project Altair is IUT's Mars rover team, competing in international rover challenges.
The rover needed four-wheel drive, a six-joint robotic arm, vision to recognise objects, and autonomous navigation.
myRole: Senior developer on the software sub-team.
Implemented the four-wheel drive and 6-joint arm control systems, as ROS nodes talking to microcontroller motor drivers.
Built inverse kinematics for precise arm manipulation.
Trained a YOLO-style object detector on a custom dataset and used its detections to drive grasping.
Built autonomous navigation with real-time obstacle avoidance.

architecture.caption: See it, reach it, grab it, drive on.

results: International Rover Challenge: 6th globally, 1st in Bangladesh, 1st in the Science Task.
Competed at the University Rover Challenge.

title: Project Aero
tagline: The drone team I led: flight control, real-time computer vision, and 3D maps built from aerial footage.

brief: Project Aero is a drone team working on flight control, navigation and aerial computer vision.
myRole: Led the team.
Worked on flight control and navigation with ArduPilot and MAVLink.
Built CV pipelines with OpenCV and YOLO for real-time object detection and tracking.
Created 3D maps of environments from drone footage using photogrammetry (structure from motion).
results: Real-time detection and tracking pipelines, plus 3D environment maps from drone footage.

title: Offline LLMs at Megamind
tagline: Fine-tuning large language models for specific jobs, then squeezing them onto hardware that isn't a data centre.

cover.alt: Diagram of the offline LLM pipeline: base LLM, fine-tuning with PEFT/LoRA, 4/8-bit quantization, offline inference with vLLM and llama.cpp, then REST APIs

brief: Megamind Tech needed large language models that work offline and fit task-specific applications.
That meant fine-tuning models and squeezing inference into resource-constrained environments.
One of the products I worked on there is [Yobo AI](https://phoneline.helloyobo.com), a phone agent for restaurants that answers calls, takes orders and handles reservations.
myRole: Fine-tuned LLMs for task-specific applications with Hugging Face Transformers and PEFT/LoRA.
Optimized offline inference with vLLM and llama.cpp, using 4/8-bit quantization to fit models on resource-constrained hardware.
Served the models behind REST inference APIs for downstream systems.

architecture.caption: From general model to task-specific, offline, behind an API.

results: Task-specific LLMs running offline on constrained hardware, served to downstream systems over REST.
